correctness.rationale: For the specified continuous-time two-action entropy-regularized Q-learning, log-odds satisfy z_i dot=−T z_i−J Σ_{j∼i}tanh(z_j/2). An entropy-augmented potential has derivative Σ_i p_i(1−p_i)(∂_i P)^2≥0 and logits stay bounded, hence omega-limits lie among equilibria. Stationary part symmetry reduces to a strictly concave positive scalar fixed-point map with derivative J²ab/(4T²) at zero; this yields exactly one equilibrium for T≥Tc=J sqrt(ab)/2 and three below. Linear Jacobian spectra establish polar stability and origin saddle; a weighted max-norm Dini inequality gives exponential contraction at exact worst-case rate T−Tc above threshold. At equality, the simple center eigenvector (sqrt b on A, −sqrt a on B) has cubic coefficient −Tc(a+b)/24, yielding generic t^{-1/2} with a stable-manifold exception and sqrt(Tc−T) polar onset. Independent cubic projections at (a,b)=(1,1),(2,5),(3,7) corroborated coefficient and sign.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General network Q-learning sufficient exploration theorems use max degree or random ensembles and do not give a necessary-and-sufficient threshold or the exact critical orbit asymptotics for arbitrary finite K_{a,b}. The 2026 Glauber spin-flip bipartite result has a different vector field, so its static phase count cannot be substituted for the logit-ODE critical rate.
